chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abdullah from Ali ibn Ja'far who said:

I heard Abu Al-Hasan (peace be upon him) saying: 'When his believing brother comes to him regarding a need, it is but a mercy from Allah, Blessed and Exalted, that He sends to him. So if he accepts that, he has been linked with our Wilayah, and he is linked with the Wilayah of Allah. And if he repels him from his need while he is able to fulfill it, Allah will cause a beast of fire to gnaw him in his grave until the Day of Resurrection, whether he is forgiven or punished. And if the petitioner accepts his excuse, his state will be even worse.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward and punishment for helping or rejecting a believer's need according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Rida (AS), the act of fulfilling a believer's need is elevated to a direct manifestation of divine mercy and a means of connecting the individual to the Wilayah of the Ahl al-Bayt. The text highlights the gravity of rejecting such a request when one is capable, warning of a 'shuja' (lion) from fire that gnaws in the grave, while noting that even with a valid excuse, the status is inferior to acceptance. This underscores the Shia emphasis on social solidarity as a core component of faith and spiritual proximity to God.
